title: enforce admin authentication on admin tool-scoring API routes
description: enforce admin authentication on admin tool-scoring API routes. `/api/admin/tools/scoring` (GET/POST/PUT) and `/api/admin/tools/scoring/recalculate` (POST) now call `requireAdmin()` from `lib/api-auth.ts` before any database access: 401 without a session, 403 for a non-admin. The same check replaces the sign-in-only check in the other `/api/admin/*` handlers that had one (articles by id, article recalculate and ingest, articles-v2, db-status, db-status-v2, rankings rollback and versions, SEO sitemap submission, image upload) and is added to the stub handlers that had none. The middleware now checks protected routes (`/:locale/admin`, `/:locale/dashboard`, `/api/admin`) before public ones, anchors public page patterns to a configured locale segment (`lib/route-access.ts`), and answers an anonymous protected `/api/*` request with a 401 JSON body instead of a sign-in redirect

title: /api/data/db-status and /api/data/articles now verify the Clerk session through requireAdmin() instead of checking that…
description: `/api/data/db-status` and `/api/data/articles` now verify the Clerk session through `requireAdmin()` instead of checking that a session cookie is present. An anonymous caller gets 401 and a signed-in non-admin gets 403, with no database details in either response. `lib/manual-auth.ts` and the unused `lib/server-actions/admin-actions.ts`, its only other caller, are removed. The what's-new summary regeneration POST and `/api/ai/analyze-news` also require an admin through `requireAdmin()`. Tests: `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`.

title: requireAdmin() and requireAuth() in lib/api-auth.ts fail closed when NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY or…
description: `requireAdmin()` and `requireAuth()` in `lib/api-auth.ts` fail closed when `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` or `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is missing in a production-like environment (`NODE_ENV=production`, or `VERCEL_ENV` of `production` or `preview`): they return 503 and never a mock user, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTH` is ignored there. The mock identities remain for local development only, with a warning. Tests: `tests/unit/api-auth-fail-closed.test.ts`.

title: POST /api/admin/articles/[id]/recalculate runs requireAdmin() before it reads the request body
description: `POST /api/admin/articles/[id]/recalculate` runs `requireAdmin()` before it reads the request body. The middleware answers an anonymous request to a protected API path with 401 regardless of the path's letter case (`/API/admin/...` used to get a sign-in redirect). `tests/unit/middleware-route-access.test.ts` now checks the exported `config.matcher` with Next's `unstable_doesMiddlewareMatch`, including bare `/api/admin`, `.json` and `.png` suffixes, an upper-case path and Clerk sign-in sub-routes.

title: the public GET /api/whats-new/summary only reads stored summaries and never starts generation
description: the public `GET /api/whats-new/summary` only reads stored summaries and never starts generation. Without a `period` it serves the current month's stored summary, else the most recent stored one; otherwise it returns 404. Generation runs only through the admin POST. `/api/data(.*)` and `/api/ai(.*)` join the middleware's protected routes, so an anonymous request is refused before the handler runs. `/api/data/db-status` reports a masked host (a short first-label prefix plus `***`) instead of the full hostname. Tests: `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`, `tests/unit/middleware-route-access.test.ts`.

title: article ingestion no longer deletes the stored what's-new summary, so a summary persists until an admin regenerates it…
description: article ingestion no longer deletes the stored what's-new summary, so a summary persists until an admin regenerates it (automatic regeneration: #160), and the empty-state copy no longer promises automatic generation. `POST /api/companies` requires an admin through `requireAdmin()`; the list GET stays public. The admin dashboard page and `GET /api/admin/articles` use `requireAdmin()`, and `lib/auth-helper.ts`, which returned a mock admin whenever `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTH` was set, is removed with the unused `lib/clerk-auth.ts`. The `/api/admin` debug routes (`debug-auth`, `test-auth`, `runtime-fix-test`, `db-test`, `bypass-test`) keep their production 404 and otherwise require an admin. The auth helpers bypass Clerk only when `NODE_ENV` is `development` or `test` and `VERCEL_ENV` is unset or `development`. `/api/data/db-status` reports a fixed `connectionError` string. Tests: `tests/unit/ingestion-keeps-summary.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-page-debug-routes-auth.test.ts`, `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-api-auth.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api-auth-fail-closed.test.ts`.

title: app/globals.css is the only global stylesheet
description: `app/globals.css` is the only global stylesheet. The stale `public/globals.css` copy is removed with its two dead readers, `components/DeferredStyles.tsx` (imported nowhere) and `app/[lang]/layout-optimized.tsx` (not a Next.js layout name, importing a missing `@/globals.css`). Pages render unchanged. A ratchet holds hard-coded colours in `components/` and `app/` at or below the #188 audit's 845 until #190 migrates them to `--ds-*` tokens. Tests: `tests/unit/globals-consolidation-189.test.ts` (#189)

title: the abandoned Payload CMS integration
description: the abandoned Payload CMS integration. `components/payload/` (`AdminDashboard.tsx`, `SubscribersManager.tsx`, `ToolsManager.tsx` and the `admin-dashboard-stats.ts` helper added in #142) had no importer anywhere in the tree — the live admin UI is `components/admin/`, whose own `AdminDashboard`, `ToolsManager` and `unified-admin-dashboard` are what the `app/[lang]/(authenticated)/` routes render — so `tests/unit/admin-dashboard-stats.test.ts` went with it, being that helper's only consumer. Two scripts that could no longer run were deleted alongside: `scripts/debug-rankings.ts` imported `payload` and `@payload-config`, neither of which exists (`payload` has never been a dependency in `package.json`, and no tsconfig path alias defines `@payload-config`), and `scripts/analyze-news-ingestion.ts` imported `lib/payload-direct`, a module absent from the repository. Both sit under the `scripts/**/*` tsconfig exclusion, which is why dangling imports survived every `tsc` run. `PAYLOAD_SECRET` is gone from `lib/env.ts`, where nothing read it, and the Payload claims in `app/api/rankings/README.md` and `app/api/tools/README.md` — which described the live routes as "Uses Payload CMS" when both read Drizzle repositories — now name the repositories those routes actually call. `hooks/use-payload.ts` and `lib/richtext-utils.ts` are kept despite their names: the first is imported by `components/admin/tools-manager.tsx` and fetches this project's own JSON API routes rather than a CMS, and the second is imported by four live files to parse stored RichText content

title: /<locale>/whats-new showed "No Monthly Summary Available" while a summary was stored
description: `/<locale>/whats-new` showed "No Monthly Summary Available" while a summary was stored. The server component fetched the relative URL `/api/whats-new/summary`; a server-side `fetch` cannot resolve a relative URL, so the read rejected and the error was swallowed. The page now reads the latest stored summary through the summary service. The empty state appears only when no summary is stored, and a failed database read shows the error page. Month and generation dates are formatted in UTC, so a server west of UTC no longer names the previous month. Tests: `tests/unit/whats-new-permalink.test.ts` (#54)

title: the ingestion gap check reported the 06:00 UTC daily run four hours late when run outside UTC
description: the ingestion gap check reported the 06:00 UTC daily run four hours late when run outside UTC. The `timestamp` columns hold UTC with no zone, and the database driver read them in the process time zone. Raw SQL readers in `scripts/` now parse them as UTC through `lib/db/naive-utc-timestamp.mjs` (`naiveUtcTypes`, `parseNaiveUtcTimestamp`) or `getRawSql()` in `lib/db/connection.ts`, so the gap, age and printed times match under any `TZ`. No schema change. `docs/deployment/cron-schedules-and-timestamps.md` records that `vercel.json` crons run on UTC. Tests: `tests/unit/naive-utc-timestamp.test.ts`, `tests/unit/naive-utc-timestamp-tz.test.ts` (#103)

title: the What's New feed and /api/changelog showed no platform changes in production
description: the What's New feed and `/api/changelog` showed no platform changes in production. `.vercelignore` matched `/*.md`, so the deploy dropped CHANGELOG.md, and `/api/changelog` answered `200 []` with no error. `npm run build` now compiles CHANGELOG.md into `data/changelog-entries.generated.json` (`npm run generate-changelog`), and the runtime imports it instead of reading the file. `[Unreleased]` entries are shown, each dated by the commit that introduced its line (the build date when none resolves). `/api/whats-new` reads these entries instead of a hardcoded 2025-10 list and holds 3 of its 20 slots for them. Both routes report `_sources` and `_degraded`; an empty module makes `/api/changelog` answer 503 instead of `200 []`. `.vercelignore` keeps CHANGELOG.md, and the `outputFileTracingIncludes` entries for it are removed. A sync test fails when the generated module is stale (#231)

title: rankings search terms no longer reach a URL or GA4 page_location
description: rankings search terms no longer reach a URL or GA4 `page_location`. The middleware answers a page GET or HEAD carrying `term`, `search`, `q`, `s`, `query` or `keyword` with a 308 to the same URL without those keys, before the auth checks; `/api` and `/_next` are untouched (`lib/search-url-keys.ts`). The rankings grid has a search box held in client state (no form, no `name`), and its badge clears the box without navigating. `site_search` fires once per settled term, 800 ms after typing stops. The schema.org SearchAction is removed from the home page and both JSON-LD builders, and `lib/search-param.ts` is deleted. Tests: `tests/unit/search-term-redaction-233.test.ts`, `tests/unit/analytics-events.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/seo-canonical-origin.test.ts` (#233)

title: /<locale>/whats-new/recent always showed the "Error / Try Again" card in production although /api/whats-new?days=7…
description: `/<locale>/whats-new/recent` always showed the "Error / Try Again" card in production although `/api/whats-new?days=7` returned items. The page built its server-side feed URL from `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, falling back to `http://localhost:3000`; the variable is unset in production, so the read went to localhost and failed. The page now builds the URL from `siteOrigin()` in `lib/site-origin.ts`. A failed read still renders the error card and an empty feed still renders "No Recent Updates" (#152) (#219)

title: two GA4 defects from the production collect capture
description: two GA4 defects from the production collect capture. (1) The rankings sort select and the sidebar feature-tag buttons sent `filter_use` and then set `window.location.href`, a full document load. gtag.js holds a hit for about five seconds before sending it, so that hit could only leave in the pagehide flush, which the capture never saw. Both controls now navigate with the App Router (`router.push`), as the sidebar category links and the `/tools` selects already did, so the page stays loaded and gtag sends the hit from its normal batch. The URL, the sort and the filter results are unchanged. (2) The rankings search term was in the `search` query key, one of the keys GA4 enhanced measurement reads as a site search, so the raw term reached GA4 as `view_search_results.search_term`. The key is now `term` (`lib/search-param.ts`) in both schema.org SearchActions (home page and root layout); the rankings page reads `term` first and still accepts `?search=` from old links, and the search badge clears both. No custom event changes name or parameters. The raw term is still in the `page_view` URL. Tests: `tests/unit/analytics-filter-delivery.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/analytics-events.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/seo-canonical-origin.test.ts` (#175)

title: /<locale>/unauthorized answers 200 instead of 500
description: `/<locale>/unauthorized` answers 200 instead of 500. The page is a Server Component and passed an `onClick` handler to its "Go Back" button, which React cannot send to the browser, so every render threw. The button is now a client component (`app/[lang]/(authenticated)/unauthorized/go-back-button.tsx`). The middleware also classes `/<locale>/unauthorized` as public (`lib/route-access.ts`), so the static page no longer triggers a session lookup; no other route changes class. Tests: `tests/unit/route-access-unauthorized-226.test.ts`, `tests/unit/unauthorized-page-226.test.tsx` (#226)

title: accessibility fixes, the first visible #190 change
description: accessibility fixes, the first visible #190 change. Light-mode rank-up text (`--ds-rank-up`) is green-700 instead of green-600, 5.02:1 on white instead of 3.30. `text-`, `bg-` and `border-destructive` classes emitted no CSS because `tailwind.config.js` had no `destructive` colour, so destructive Alerts, the home autonomous-agent card, the error-boundary icon and the confirm-dialog button had no red; `destructive` now resolves to `--ds-danger`, with `--ds-surface` as the fill foreground. `--ds-border-strong` reaches 3:1 on every surface in both modes, and form-control edges (Input, Select, Textarea, the outline button, admin selects, the subscribe checkbox; 10 sites) use it instead of `border-input`; `--ds-border` stays a decorative exception. Success and warning modifier text in the rankings and comparison tables uses the mode-dependent `--ds-success` / `--ds-warning` (5.02:1 light, 11.48 / 11.98 dark; was 3.30 / 3.56 light); the unused `--ds-success-fixed` and `--ds-warning-fixed` move to the 700 step. `/design` answers 404 in production unless `DESIGN_PREVIEW` is set, and shows Alert, form-control and modifier-text samples. Tests: `tests/unit/tailwind-colour-classes-190.test.ts` (fails on a colour class that compiles to nothing), `tests/unit/design-contrast-190.test.ts`, `tests/unit/design-tokens-178.test.ts`, `tests/unit/modifier-text-contrast-190.test.ts`, `tests/unit/design-page-190.test.tsx` (#190)

title: the quality assessment step failed open
description: the quality assessment step failed open. An unparseable reply fell back to default scores with no error, so the candidate was counted as `quality_rejected` and a run in which no reply parsed still ended `completed` with a 200. An unparseable reply now yields an assessment carrying `error`, logged at error level, and the candidate is recorded as `assessment_failed`; replies are parsed with the shared `extractJsonObject()`. When every assessed candidate fails assessment, the run ends `failed` and `/api/cron/daily-news` answers 500. A reply with no numeric score (such as `{}`) is an assessment failure too, and the batch circuit breaker no longer accepts the remaining candidates at score 7 once more than 30% of assessments fail: it skips them as `assessment_failed`. The assessment budget rises from 1,000 to 2,000 completion tokens. `CHANGELOG.md` now ships with the routes that read it (`outputFileTracingIncludes`), so the cron run no longer logs an ENOENT error for it. Tests: `lib/services/article-quality.service.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cron-daily-news-billing.test.ts` (#172)

title: article analysis on anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 failed with "AI response was not valid JSON"
description: article analysis on `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` failed with "AI response was not valid JSON". The analysis request now allows 8,000 completion tokens (was 4,000) and its JSON template no longer carries `//` comments. Every OpenRouter call site that uses `getOpenRouterModel()` reads `finish_reason`: a reply cut off at `max_tokens` fails as "AI response truncated at the token limit", is not retried, and a truncated what's-new or State of AI summary is not stored. Each completion logs its finish_reason, content length, token counts and model id, never the content. JSON replies are parsed from the first complete object, so a code fence or a sentence of prose around it no longer fails the parse; a cut-off object is still rejected. Tests: `lib/services/llm-completion.test.ts`, `tests/unit/ai-analyzer-truncation.test.ts` (#172)

title: OpenRouter retired anthropic/claude-sonnet-4, so every call answered 404 "No endpoints found" and the 2026-10-19…
description: OpenRouter retired `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`, so every call answered 404 "No endpoints found" and the 2026-10-19 daily-news cron run returned 500. Article analysis, quality assessment, the what's-new and State of AI summaries and the admin news analyzer now take their model from `getOpenRouterModel()` in `lib/services/openrouter-model.ts`: `OPENROUTER_MODEL` when set, else `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. Ingested articles record the model id actually called instead of the fixed label "Claude 4 Sonnet". Tests: `tests/unit/openrouter-model.test.ts` (#172)

title: daily-news ingestion now fails the run and the cron returns 500 when a provider (Tavily, Jina, OpenRouter) rejects a…
description: daily-news ingestion now fails the run and the cron returns 500 when a provider (Tavily, Jina, OpenRouter) rejects a call for billing or credit reasons, instead of recording a completed run with 0 articles; the gap detector raises `PROVIDER_BILLING` and matches OpenRouter's "requires more credits" text (#167)

title: /sitemap.xml listed no news articles and no tool pages for up to an hour after every deploy
description: `/sitemap.xml` listed no news articles and no tool pages for up to an hour after every deploy. `next build` prerendered `app/sitemap.ts` while `getDb()` refuses to connect (`NEXT_PHASE=phase-production-build`), so the deployed sitemap held the 55 static URLs only until its first ISR revalidation, and a failed read at request time was cached the same way for the full hour. The sitemap is now the route handler `app/sitemap.xml/route.ts` (`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`), read from the database per request and cached by the CDN with `s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`; each active article is listed once as `/en/news/<slug>` with its publication date as `<lastmod>`. A failed database read answers 503 with `Cache-Control: no-store` instead of an article-less sitemap (#162)

title: when the database read failed, /api/news answered 200 with news: [], because NewsRepository.getPaginatedFiltered() and…
description: when the database read failed, `/api/news` answered 200 with `news: []`, because `NewsRepository.getPaginatedFiltered()` and `countFiltered()` turned any error into an empty result; `/api/news/recent` did the same through `getRecentWithin()`. All three now throw, including when no database is configured, and both routes answer a failed read with a 503 carrying `Cache-Control: no-store` and an error body. A read that matches nothing is still a 200 with an empty list. Successful responses were never stored at the edge: `lib/api-cache.ts` gave `/api/news*` `max-age=0` and `must-revalidate`, then appended `no-cache` (and `no-store, private` for mobile User-Agents) plus `Vary: User-Agent`. They now carry `public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=1800`. The same helper stops setting an `ETag` that was identical on every response (it hashed a stream that stringifies to `{}`) and an `X-Vercel-Cache: MISS` header that masked Vercel's own. The news page and the home page news card stop appending per-request `cb`/`_r`/`_ua` query parameters, which made every fetch a cache miss, and the now-unused `lib/api/cache-busting.ts` is deleted. A `?debug=true` response, which echoes the caller's User-Agent, is `no-store`. `/api/whats-new` had the same bug through `NewsRepository.getPaginated()`: a failed news read gave a 200 feed of tools and changelog entries with no news, cached for a minute. It now reads `getPageFiltered()` and answers a failed news read with a 503 `no-store`, even when the tools read succeeded, because the feed is one merged list with no per-section marker; any other failure is a 500 `no-store`, and a successful response keeps `public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60`. `getPaginated()` had no other caller and is removed. The news page now shows an error card with a "Try Again" button (`common.error` / `common.tryAgain` from the dictionary) when `/api/news` fails, and keeps the "no news items" card for a successful empty read; the read moves to `components/news/load-news.ts`. The two other readers of `/api/whats-new`, the `/{lang}/whats-new/recent` page and the What's New modal, also turned a failed read (a non-2xx or a network error) into an empty feed and showed "No Recent Updates"; both now show the same error card and "Try Again" button (a reload link on the server-rendered page, a refetch in the modal) and keep the empty state for a successful empty feed. The page's read stays `no-store`. All three readers share `loadList()` in `lib/load-list.ts`. Tests: `tests/unit/news-route-fail-closed.test.ts`, `tests/unit/whats-new-route-fail-closed.test.ts`, `tests/unit/news-content-load.test.ts`, `tests/unit/whats-new-feed-load.test.ts`, `lib/db/repositories/news.test.ts` (#152)

title: every non-English page except home, rankings and trending declared the English page as its canonical — /de/news emitted…
description: every non-English page except home, rankings and trending declared the English page as its canonical — `/de/news` emitted `<link rel="canonical" href="https://aipowerranking.com/en/news">` — which tells search engines to drop the translation, although each locale is a real one. `localizedAlternates()` in `lib/seo/alternates.ts` loses its `canonicalLang` option, so every page it builds is now self-canonical (`/de/news` → `https://aipowerranking.com/de/news`), and its hreflang set gains `x-default` pointing at the page's `/en` URL next to the 10 locales from `i18n/config.ts`. `lib/seo/utils.ts`, behind the tool detail and the four dashboard pages, had its own hreflang map with a `pt-BR` → `/pt` locale the site does not serve and a canonical and `og:url` without the locale segment (`https://aipowerranking.com/tools/cursor`); it now takes the page's `lang` and builds both from the same helper. The dashboard pages declared `/admin`, `/admin/tools` and `/admin/dashboard` although they are served at `/{lang}/dashboard`, `/{lang}/dashboard/tools` and `/{lang}/dashboard/dashboard`; each now reads its locale in `generateMetadata` and names its real route. The trending page gains the `og:url` it lacked, so `og:url` equals the canonical on every page. `generateRankingMetadata()` and `generateComparisonMetadata()`, which had no callers and named routes that do not exist, are deleted. The sitemap emits no per-URL alternates. Review follow-up: a `noIndex` page built by `lib/seo/utils.ts` (the four dashboard pages) keeps its canonical and RSS link but emits no hreflang, since it offers nothing to index; an unknown locale segment such as `/xx/news` or `/EN/tools/cursor`, which renders the English page, now canonicalises to the `/en` URL instead of to itself; `lib/seo/utils.ts` sets `og:locale` to the page locale instead of `en_US`; and `lib/markdown-page-utils.ts`, which nothing imported, is deleted. Second follow-up: on an unknown locale segment, `og:url` and the RSS link now follow the canonical to English too. The 17 hand-built page metadata blocks take `openGraph.url` from `localizedAlternates(lang, path).canonical` instead of rebuilding it from `lang`, and `newsRssAlternateTypes()`, which `app/[lang]/layout.tsx` also uses, falls back through the new `canonicalLocale()`, so `/xx/news` advertises `/en/news/rss.xml` instead of a feed that returns 404. The rule: a page whose main body is English in every locale is a duplicate of its `/en` page, not a translation, so every locale canonicalises to the `/en` URL, with `og:url` the same, `og:locale` `en`, no hreflang or `x-default` (a cross-language canonical next to hreflang is a conflicting signal), and the page locale's RSS link kept; only a page with real per-locale body content (home, rankings, trending, tools, tool detail) self-canonicalises with the full hreflang set. Translated navigation does not make a page per-locale; its main body decides. The English-only pages are news articles and the news list (English-only news and State of AI APIs), about, methodology, terms, privacy and contact (markdown from `lib/content-loader.ts`, which falls back to `src/content/en/` because no other locale directory exists), the nine best-* guides (English literals, no dictionary) and both what's-new pages (English literals and API). The policy lives in `englishOnlyAlternates()` and `ENGLISH_ONLY_OG_LOCALE` in `lib/seo/alternates.ts`. `app/sitemap.ts` lists each English-only page, articles included, once under `/en` instead of under all 10 locales, and names the contact page's canonical `/en/contact/default` instead of `/{lang}/contact`, which only redirects. The terms, privacy, contact and both what's-new pages, which emitted no canonical and inherited the root layout's `og:url` of `/`, now carry canonical alternates and a matching `og:url`; the what's-new alternates sit on each page, since a layout-level canonical would name the index for its child. The unknown-segment fallback also reaches the home page's WebSite JSON-LD, the tool detail breadcrumb and `og:locale` on the home, trending and `lib/seo/utils.ts` pages; third follow-up: the rankings and tools list pages set their own `openGraph` with no `locale`, so `/de/rankings` and `/de/tools` fell back to the root layout's `en_US` — both now set `openGraph.locale` to `canonicalLocale(lang)`, matching home and trending (#156)

title: /en/news and every other page that sets its own canonical served no <link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">
description: `/en/news` and every other page that sets its own canonical served no `<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml">`. `app/[lang]/layout.tsx` advertises the feed under `alternates.types`, and Next.js replaces the whole `alternates` object when a page sets one. `localizedAlternates()` in `lib/seo/alternates.ts` now takes the page's locale and adds `types["application/rss+xml"]` for `${siteOrigin()}/${lang}/news/rss.xml`, built by `newsRssAlternateTypes()`, which the layout also uses — so the news list and article pages, home, rankings, trending, tools, tool detail, about, methodology and the nine category pages all keep the link (#155)

title: on Vercel every page's <link rel="canonical">, every hrefLang alternate, the openGraph URLs and the JSON-LD named the…
description: on Vercel every page's `<link rel="canonical">`, every `hrefLang` alternate, the openGraph URLs and the JSON-LD named the per-deployment `*.vercel.app` host, telling search engines the real domain was a duplicate. Pages built these URLs from `getUrl()`, which returns `https://${VERCEL_URL}`, and the root layout's `metadataBase` did the same. All SEO-facing URLs — `metadataBase`, canonical, hreflang, openGraph/twitter URLs, the JSON-LD in `app/layout.tsx`, the home, rankings and tool pages and `lib/seo/schema.ts`, `lib/seo/utils.ts`, the OG-image helpers, sitemap, robots and sitemap submission — now come from `siteOrigin()` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, else `https://aipowerranking.com`). Localized pages build `alternates` through one helper, `localizedAlternates()` in `lib/seo/alternates.ts`; the trending page's relative alternates and the rankings page's canonical-only alternates now carry absolute URLs and a full hreflang set. `getUrl()` still returns the deployment's own host for the server-side `/api/*` fetches in the news article and rankings pages, and its production fallback no longer misspells the domain as `aipowerrankings.com`. `lib/seo/schema.ts` read `A || B ? https://${VERCEL_URL} : ""`, which parses as `(A || B) ? …`; each builder now reads the origin at call time. `lib/get-base-url.ts`, whose only callers were the two SEO modules, is deleted (#153)

title: /{lang}/news/rss.xml returned 404 although every locale page advertised it as its RSS alternate and the news page…
description: `/{lang}/news/rss.xml` returned 404 although every locale page advertised it as its RSS alternate and the news page linked to it. A route at `app/[lang]/news/rss.xml/route.ts` now serves an RSS 2.0 feed for each locale in `i18n/config.ts` (404 for any other): one channel with title, link, description, language, `lastBuildDate` and an `atom:link rel="self"`, and the 50 newest active articles, each with title, localized article link, permalink guid, RFC 822 `pubDate` and description. All text is entity-escaped, including `>`, so a `]]>` in an article cannot break the document. Articles come from a new `NewsRepository.getPageFiltered()` — the page query `getPaginatedFiltered()` (and so `/api/news` and the news page) already ran, now factored out and delegated to — which throws on a failed read instead of returning an empty page; the feed turns that into a `no-store` 503, never an empty 200 the CDN would cache. Responses carry `Content-Type: application/rss+xml; charset=utf-8` and `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=1800`, the CDN window `/api/news` uses (#150)

title: the RSS alternate advertised by app/[lang]/layout.tsx pointed at the per-deployment *.vercel.app host on Vercel and at…
description: the RSS alternate advertised by `app/[lang]/layout.tsx` pointed at the per-deployment `*.vercel.app` host on Vercel and at `https://undefined/...` elsewhere when only `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` was set — `A || B ? x : ""` parses as `(A || B) ? x : ""`. The layout and the feed now take their origin from one helper, `siteOrigin()` in `lib/site-origin.ts`: `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` if set, else `https://aipowerranking.com`, the rule `app/sitemap.ts` and `app/robots.ts` already follow. The feed's channel link, self link, item links and guids no longer come from `getUrl()` or the request host, so guids stay the same across deploys (#150)

title: npm run build runs generate-categories before next build, and with no DATABASE_URL that script rewrote the committed…
description: `npm run build` runs `generate-categories` before `next build`, and with no `DATABASE_URL` that script rewrote the committed `lib/data/static-categories.ts` down to a single "All Categories" entry with a fresh `Generated:` timestamp and exited 0 — a developer who built locally and committed wiped 57 lines of category data behind a diff that looked routine. Two swallowed failures caused it: `fetchCategoriesFromDb()` caught every connection and query error and returned the placeholder as if it were a real read, and a snapshot with no rankings row produced that same placeholder. Both now propagate. `scripts/generate-static-categories.ts` keeps only environment, database and filesystem access; the write/skip/fail decision moves to `lib/data/static-categories-generator.ts` as a pure async function over injected dependencies (`hasDatabaseUrl`, `allowEmpty`, `fetchCategories`, `writeFile`, `log`, `logError`) returning the exit code, so every branch is reachable from `tests/unit/generate-static-categories.test.ts` with no database. The matrix: no connection string configured prints one line saying regeneration is skipped and the committed file is kept, touches nothing and exits 0, so local builds keep working; a connection or query error prints the message with any `postgres://` / `postgresql://` URL redacted (this repository is public and the build log is not private), touches nothing and exits 1; a read of zero categories prints that the file was left untouched and exits 1 unless `--allow-empty` is passed, which writes the empty result and exits 0; a read of one or more categories writes as before. The write itself is now atomic — a temp file beside the target, then a rename — so a crash mid-write cannot leave the module truncated. The guard asks `hasUsableDatabaseUrl()` in `lib/db/connection.ts` rather than reading `process.env` a second time, so it cannot disagree with what `getDb()` will do. Vercel is unaffected: `DATABASE_URL` is set there, so the build regenerates the file exactly as it did (#143)

title: review follow-up on the above
description: review follow-up on the above. The generate-categories guard first mirrored `getDatabaseUrl()` by ORing `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_URL_DEVELOPMENT` and `DATABASE_URL_STAGING`, but that function is conditioned on `NODE_ENV` and in production — which is what a Vercel build runs as — reads `DATABASE_URL` only. An environment carrying just `DATABASE_URL_STAGING` therefore passed the guard, reached `getDb()`, and threw, turning a skip into a failed build. The branching rules move to `lib/db/database-url.ts` as `resolveDatabaseUrl(env, nodeEnv)` — a pure function reading no globals — which `getDatabaseUrl()` now calls (its four log lines are reconstructed by `describeDatabaseUrlResolution` from the same result, so `getDb()`'s output is unchanged) and which the new exported `hasUsableDatabaseUrl()` wraps for the script. The script's own variable list is deleted. Because the resolver takes its environment as an argument, `tests/unit/generate-static-categories.test.ts` drives every `NODE_ENV` without mutating `process.env` and without importing the connection module, whose import runs dotenv — so the tests depend on no `.env*` file existing (#143)

title: every card on components/payload/AdminDashboard.tsx showed 0
description: every card on `components/payload/AdminDashboard.tsx` showed 0. The component read `totalDocs` from `/api/news`, `/api/tools` and `/api/rankings`, and `docs[0].period` for the ranking period — the Payload CMS collection shape, which none of these routes has ever returned, so all four values fell through `|| 0` and rendered a zero indistinguishable from a real count. `/api/admin/subscribers` made it worse: no route implements that path, so it answered 404 with an HTML body, `.json()` threw, and because all four fetches shared one `try` the throw skipped the single `setStats` call — every card stayed at its initial zero even for the three endpoints that had answered fine. Each response is now read independently through a helper that returns `null` on a non-2xx status or an unparseable body, and each count comes from the field its route actually emits: `total` for news, the length of the returned `tools` array (the route takes no parameters and returns every active tool), and `stats.total_tools` plus top-level `period` for rankings. A count that could not be read renders an em dash rather than 0, so "no rows" and "could not reach the endpoint" stay distinguishable. "Last Generated" displayed `new Date()` — today's date, whatever had actually happened — and now reads the snapshot's `published_at` as "Rankings Published", falling back to "N/A" on the no-rankings-yet branch, which omits that field. The response-to-count mapping moves into `components/payload/admin-dashboard-stats.ts` as a pure function over one interface per endpoint; the interfaces declare no `totalDocs`, so a repeat of this typo is a `tsc` error rather than a silent zero (#140 follow-up)

title: /api/news?limit=100&offset=300 returned news: [] and a total of 300
description: `/api/news?limit=100&offset=300` returned `news: []` and a `total` of 300. The route fetched a fixed `getPaginated(limit * 3, 0)` pool, classified each row's `event_type` in JavaScript, then filtered and `.slice(offset, offset + limit)`d that pool — so no offset past the pool could resolve and `total` was the pool length, not the count. `event_type` was the only reason the pool existed and it is not a stored column, so the keyword ladders it was derived from move into SQL (`lib/db/news-event-type.ts`, one `CASE` cascade over `tags` then `title || summary-or-content`, same rung order); the SELECT list, the `WHERE` and the `COUNT(*)` now read that one expression, and nothing is filtered after the fetch. `NewsRepository` gains `getPaginatedFiltered()` and `countFiltered()` — real `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, a real `COUNT(*)`, and `id` breaking `published_date` ties so a row cannot repeat on one page and vanish from the next — with `getPaginated()` left for its other callers. `limit` is clamped to 100 and `offset` floored at 0, and a non-numeric value falls back to the default instead of reaching the statement as NaN. `/api/news/recent` had the same shape: it fetched the top 100 by published date and applied `days` in memory, silently truncating any window holding more than 100 articles — the lower bound, the ordering and the bound are now one query over `COALESCE(published_date, created_at)`. Response shapes, cache headers and the per-item `event_type` the news page filters on client-side are unchanged (#140)

title: migration 0013_add_candidate_outcome_tracking.sql shipped with the #133 deploy and was never applied, so production…
description: migration `0013_add_candidate_outcome_tracking.sql` shipped with the #133 deploy and was never applied, so production ingestion was down from 2026-09-04 — migrations are applied by hand and nobody can pull a production `DATABASE_URL` to a laptop. A dispatchable **Apply database migration** workflow (`.github/workflows/apply-migration.yml`) runs the apply from CI against the existing `DATABASE_URL` repository secret, the same one `cron-gap-detector.yml` already queries production with: dispatch once with `dry_run: true` to see the on-disk files, the ones recorded in `_drizzle_migrations` and the target table's columns without writing anything, then again with `dry_run: false` to apply exactly the named file. `scripts/apply-migrations.ts` gains the `--dry-run`, `--only <file>`, `--force` and `--show-columns <table>` flags behind it; `--only` refuses non-zero on a filename that is missing or already recorded rather than re-running its statements, `--force` (valid only alongside `--only`) lifts that second refusal for the one named file and keeps its existing tracking row rather than inserting a second — the escape hatch for a migration the old splitter recorded without executing, `--dry-run` does not even create the tracking table, and every message is stripped of anything URL-shaped so a driver error cannot carry the connection string into this public repository's Actions log. The statement splitter is also fixed: it dropped any chunk whose first characters were `--`, which meant applying 0013 executed neither of its `ALTER TABLE`s while still recording the file as applied — both sit under a leading comment line. Workflow inputs are shape-checked in shell and reach it only through `env:` mapping (#134)

title: the 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06 cron runs returned HTTP 200 but wrote no row to automated_ingestion_runs, logging column…
description: the 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06 cron runs returned HTTP 200 but wrote no row to `automated_ingestion_runs`, logging `column "articles_skipped_stale" of relation "automated_ingestion_runs" does not exist`. #133 added `articles_skipped_stale` and `candidate_outcomes` to the Drizzle schema and shipped migration 0013, which is applied by hand and had not been run before the deploy. `updateRun()` already retried without the two columns, but `createRun()` ran first and had no such path. Leaving the columns out of `.values()` did not keep them out of the statement — Drizzle's insert builder names every column of the table and passes `default` for the omitted ones, and a bare `.returning()` lists them all a second time, so both halves referenced columns the database lacked. `createRun()` now seeds the row through an explicit column list and returns only `id`, writing the same values it wrote before; a remaining undefined-column error retries once on `run_type`/`status`/`started_at` and lets the database defaults fill the rest, and any other error still propagates (#134)

title: review follow-up on the gap-detector fallback trigger — three ways it could fire or leak when it should not
description: review follow-up on the gap-detector fallback trigger — three ways it could fire or leak when it should not. `createRun()` takes no lock and run 483bd3e8 sat at `status='running'` permanently, so `check-ingestion-gap.mjs` now ends every outcome with `LAST_STATUS=` and `LAST_RUN_STARTED=` lines and the workflow refuses to call production while the latest row is still `running` (a second pipeline would run concurrently against the same tables); the gap check still goes red. `STALLED` is evaluated independently of the other three conditions, so it can co-occur with `RUN_FAILED`/`OPENROUTER_CREDITS`/`ZERO_YIELD_STREAK` — which mean the cron *is* firing; those now suppress the trigger and the issue names which one did. When the fallback call returns 2xx and the re-check still fails, the reason line distinguishes "wrote a row and that run then failed" (a non-STALLED alert in the re-check) from "wrote nothing" (still STALLED at the same `LAST_RUN_STARTED`), instead of asserting the latter in both cases. Auto-close now matches the issue title as well as the `ingestion-alert` label, so a human-labeled unrelated issue is left open. The response body no longer reaches the issue raw: this repository is public and the route's 500 path returns `error.message` verbatim, so only a JSON `error` string survives, with token-shaped runs and anything after `key`/`token`/`secret`/`bearer` replaced by `[redacted]` before a 200-character cap — a non-JSON body (an HTML error page, a proxy banner) is dropped entirely (#134)

title: the ingestion gap detector could only report that no run row had landed; it could not tell a Vercel scheduler that…
description: the ingestion gap detector could only report that no run row had landed; it could not tell a Vercel scheduler that never fired from one that fired and got a silent 401, which is the distinction the 2026-09-04 stall (#134) turned on. On `ALERT[STALLED]` only — never on `RUN_FAILED`/`OPENROUTER_CREDITS`/`ZERO_YIELD_STREAK`/`NO_RUNS_EVER`, where the cron is demonstrably firing — the workflow now calls `GET $PRODUCTION_BASE_URL/api/cron/daily-news` from the runner with the `CRON_SECRET` repository secret, then re-runs `scripts/check-ingestion-gap.mjs` (the same query, not a second copy of the SQL) and records the verdict in the alert issue: a 401 means GitHub's secret and Vercel Production's have diverged, a 2xx plus a fresh row is a recovery, a 2xx with no new row means the route returned success and wrote nothing. With no `CRON_SECRET` configured the call is skipped and the issue says so. A `force_trigger` dispatch input runs the same call on demand, replacing `scripts/trigger-ingestion.ts` as the backfill path. The workflow also closes every open `ingestion-alert` issue once the check passes, and the STALLED remediation text now walks the Vercel Cron Jobs tab and function logs instead of asserting a redeploy as the recurring root cause — repo history records no case of a redeploy fixing a stall. `app/api/cron/daily-news` gains its first tests, pinning that an unauthorized request never constructs `AutomatedIngestionService` and that an unset `CRON_SECRET` cannot be satisfied by an empty bearer (#134)

title: the 2026-09-03 06:00 UTC run ingested three articles the same day with published_date of Aug 20, Aug 21 and Aug 30, so…
description: the 2026-09-03 06:00 UTC run ingested three articles the same day with `published_date` of Aug 20, Aug 21 and Aug 30, so `/api/news/recent?days=1` returned nothing and the gap detector saw a healthy run. Every freshness mechanism keyed off Tavily's self-reported date, and nothing recorded that the `time_range=day` recency pass (#125) had found a result. Search results now carry `discoveredVia` (recency/window) and dedupe by that tag rather than by array position; the freshness gate never drops a recency-pass candidate for a stale provider date, and the freshest-first sort orders on a provisional date (the provider date when it is inside the window, else the run's discovery time for a recency candidate). At insert, a deterministic resolver replaces `metadata.publishedDate || analysis.published_date` — the LLM-extracted article date wins when it parses, is not future-dated, and is inside the window; then the provider date; then, for a recency candidate only, the run's discovery time; else the previous fallback — and records which rule won as `publishedDateSource` on the article's processing log. The run row gains `articles_skipped_stale` (opportunistic fix: the count was computed every run but `updateRun` never mapped it and no column existed, so it was silently dropped) and `candidate_outcomes`, a capped per-candidate list of URL, pass, dates, outcome and reason, so "a fresh candidate existed and failed to insert" is distinguishable from "no fresh candidate existed". Both write only through `updateRun`, and a write that predates migration 0013 retries without them so the terminal status and existing counters still land (#132)

title: a 429-triggered auto-block (extended in #127) never expired — it shared the same permanent-for-process-life semantics…
description: a 429-triggered auto-block (extended in #127) never expired — it shared the same permanent-for-process-life semantics as a 401/403/"blocked" refusal, so one rate-limited run could starve an otherwise-healthy source for the rest of a warm serverless process. A 429-only trigger now records a 4-hour TTL (`AUTO_BLOCK_TTL_MS`); `isDomainBlocked()` treats an expired entry as unblocked and evicts it lazily on read. 401/403/"blocked" triggers are unchanged (#126)

title: a pipeline that hit PIPELINE_TIMEOUT_MS and was marked status='failed' could still have its own abandoned,…
description: a pipeline that hit `PIPELINE_TIMEOUT_MS` and was marked `status='failed'` could still have its own abandoned, still-running `executeDailyDiscovery` call overwrite that row later with a stale `completed`/`partial` and a reset `completedAt` — `runDailyDiscovery`'s `Promise.race` never cancels the losing side. `updateRun()` now guards any write carrying a terminal `status` with `WHERE status = 'running'` in the same UPDATE, so a write that loses the race matches zero rows and is silently skipped instead of downgrading an already-terminal row; counter-only checkpoint writes stay unguarded and continue to apply (#128)

title: the "Referenced Links" section on article pages could carry the source site's own footer/sister-site navigation instead…
description: the "Referenced Links" section on article pages could carry the source site's own footer/sister-site navigation instead of story references (e.g. an Insurance Journal article listing mynewmarkets.com, claimsjournal.com, insurancejournal.tv, ijacademy.com, carriermanagement.com) — none share the source article's domain, so a same-domain filter alone could not catch them. The ingestion prompt now instructs the model to include only links that are directly story-relevant and actually appear in the source, allowing an empty block; a new deterministic `sanitizeRelatedLinksBlock()` independently verifies each link the model returns against the actual source content/hrefs it was shown and drops anything unverifiable or shaped like nav/footer chrome, applied at ingestion time for new articles. A render-time `filterChromeLinks()` heuristic (anchor-text/domain matching, no access to the original source) also runs on every article's display, including already-stored ones, as a best-effort backstop (#122)

title: a run row could stay stuck status='running' with all counters at 0 even after articles were successfully ingested under…
description: a run row could stay stuck `status='running'` with all counters at 0 even after articles were successfully ingested under it (seen on run 483bd3e8, 2026-08-29) — every finalization write funneled through a single `updateRun()` call per exit branch, each with its own log-and-swallow catch and no retry, so one failed write (e.g. a dropped DB connection near a serverless timeout) abandoned the row forever with the gap-detector unable to see it. Persistence is now centralized into one retrying, never-throwing `finalizeRun()` helper called from a single `finally` block covering every exit path, plus a checkpoint write of the accrued counters immediately after the ingest loop so a failure later in the pipeline can no longer leave the row at all-zero (#124)

title: discovery could go days without surfacing same-day content — Tavily ranks by relevance, not recency, so a same-day…
description: discovery could go days without surfacing same-day content — Tavily ranks by relevance, not recency, so a same-day story could rank below several-days-old ones and miss the result cutoff entirely, and the two `maxArticles` caps downstream then truncated in that relevance order rather than by freshness. Discovery now issues an explicit `time_range: 'day'` recency pass alongside the existing days-bounded pass (additive, not narrowing), and all candidates are sorted freshest-source-date-first before either cap so a same-day item can no longer be crowded out by an older, higher-relevance one (#125)

title: extraction failures from a source that rate-limits (HTTP 429, e.g
description: extraction failures from a source that rate-limits (HTTP 429, e.g. `devin.ai`) are now treated the same as 401/403/"blocked" and auto-block the domain for the rest of the run. Root cause went deeper than the missing 429 case: `TavilyExtractService.extractContent()` swallowed its own error and returned `null` after exhausting retries, so the auto-block check downstream never received the provider's error text for ANY status code — it now throws once retries are exhausted (matching `JinaReaderService`'s existing behavior), and the auto-block check moved to the extraction-chain catch blocks that actually observe it (#125)

title: article detail pages rendered the same links twice — an in-body "Related Links" block and a "Referenced Links" section…
description: article detail pages rendered the same links twice — an in-body "Related Links" block and a "Referenced Links" section beneath it, with identical content. Both came from one field: the ingestion prompt appends a `**Related Links:**` markdown block to `rewritten_content`, which rendered as prose, while the detail component separately regex-extracted every markdown link out of that same string. The in-body block is now stripped before the prose is rendered, so "Referenced Links" is the page's only links section; extraction still reads the original content, so the surviving list stays populated for already-stored articles. Repeated URLs are also deduplicated by URL

title: freshness gate — an auto-discovered article whose SOURCE published date is older than FRESHNESS_WINDOW_DAYS (default…
description: freshness gate — an auto-discovered article whose SOURCE published date is older than `FRESHNESS_WINDOW_DAYS` (default 14) is now skipped before any extraction or LLM spend, and never counts toward `articlesIngested`. Since ~2026-08-20 every discovered article carried a date weeks to months old, so runs inserted rows and reported healthy positive yield while nothing surfaced in any publishedDate-ordered or -filtered view (recent news, sitemap top, the monthly editorial's month window). A run that discovers articles but yields zero fresh ones now records `articles_ingested = 0` against a positive `articles_discovered`, so the existing `ZERO_YIELD_STREAK` alert in `scripts/check-ingestion-gap.mjs` fires

title: the daily cron called runDailyDiscovery() with no arguments, so the Tavily days lookback was undefined and omitted from…
description: the daily cron called `runDailyDiscovery()` with no arguments, so the Tavily `days` lookback was `undefined` and omitted from the request — discovery was relevance-ranked with no date bound at all. It now defaults to the freshness window; an explicit `--days` still wins and widens the gate in step

title: each stored monthly report has a permanent URL, /<locale>/whats-new/<YYYY-MM>
description: each stored monthly report has a permanent URL, `/<locale>/whats-new/<YYYY-MM>`. The page shows the month as its heading, the report, and links to the other stored reports. It canonicalises to `/en/whats-new/<YYYY-MM>` in every locale, with the month in the title, the report's first sentence as the description, and one JSON-LD `Article` block. A malformed period or a month with no stored report is a 404, never the latest report; a failed database read is an error. The sitemap lists each stored report once, under `/en`, and a failed period read is a 503 like the other sitemap reads. The `/whats-new` index links to the latest report's permalink and canonicalises to it while a report exists. Tests: `tests/unit/whats-new-permalink.test.ts`, `tests/unit/sitemap-route.test.ts`, `tests/unit/seo-canonical-origin.test.ts` (#54)

title: a rankings search that matches no tool now shows "No tools match "<term>"." (announced as a status message) with a…
description: a rankings search that matches no tool now shows "No tools match "<term>"." (announced as a status message) with a "Clear search" button, instead of a blank grid. The button clears the box without navigating. No message appears while rankings load, for an empty term, or for a category filter alone; `site_search` is unchanged. The text comes from the new `rankings.noResults` and `rankings.clearSearch` keys in all ten locales. The unused `components/analytics/GoogleAnalytics-optimized.tsx` loader is deleted; the live `GoogleAnalytics.tsx` stays. Tests: `tests/unit/rankings-empty-state-207.test.tsx` (#207)

title: record the partial #174 GA4 baseline from the static Pages and screens export in docs/refresh/analytics-baseline-174.md
description: record the partial #174 GA4 baseline from the static Pages and screens export in `docs/refresh/analytics-baseline-174.md`. 0 of 6 acceptance criteria are met, so the bot-share gate stays unfrozen; list-to-detail uses a page-view proxy until the #175 `ranking_row_click` event has data (#174)

title: tool icons and tier badges move to tokens and meet contrast (#190 C2, Option B)
description: tool icons and tier badges move to tokens and meet contrast (#190 C2, Option B). `ToolIcon`'s nine gradient fills use the new HSL `--ds-grad-*` tokens; green, orange and teal darken from the 500-600 to the 700-800 steps, so the white glyph is 5.02, 5.18 and 5.47:1 (was 2.28, 2.80, 2.49). `TierLegend` and `getTierColor` drop the S-D gradients for the solid `--ds-score-*` bands with `--ds-score-fg` text: white on 5.02-7.58:1 fills in light mode, near-black on 7.23-11.98:1 fills in dark mode (the S tier was 1.92:1); a tier badge keeps its band on hover instead of taking Badge's default blue hover fill. The ranking cards, tier legend and tool lists change colour on every page that shows them. The home page's Autonomous Agents card drops `destructive`, which has rendered error red since C1, for the new purple `--ds-accent-agent` (purple-700 light, purple-400 dark) on its link text, count badge and hover border: the link text is 6.98:1 on the card and the badge text 5.92:1 on its 10% tint in light mode, 7.57 and 6.78:1 in dark mode. Alerts, the error boundary and destructive buttons stay red. `/design` shows the shipped fills and the purple card with their ratios. The hard-coded colour ratchet falls from 707 to 679. Tests: `tests/unit/design-options-190.test.ts`, `tests/unit/tier-badge-hover-190.test.ts`, `tests/unit/agent-card-accent-190.test.ts` (#190)

title: every daily-news ingestion run logs one [AutomatedIngestion] Run summary line with its status, a fixed failure-cause…
description: every daily-news ingestion run logs one `[AutomatedIngestion] Run summary` line with its status, a fixed failure-cause label and the stage counts: discovered, stale, candidates, URL and semantic duplicates, fetched, fetch-failed, blocked-domain, assessed, assessment-failed, rejected, passed-quality, added and ingest-failed. The line carries counts only. A failed run, including the fail-closed assessment path and the pipeline timeout, logs it at error level before the route answers 500; any other run logs it at warn. Tests: `tests/unit/cron-daily-news-billing.test.ts`, `tests/unit/ingestion-run-summary.test.ts` (#172)

title: a /design state sheet showing card, table, badge, nav, footer, score pill and rank change in each state, in a light…
description: a `/design` state sheet showing card, table, badge, nav, footer, score pill and rank change in each state, in a light panel and a `.dark` panel. It is `noindex`, linked from nowhere and not in the sitemap. Hover and focus samples use the components' own CSS through `data-force-state`. `npm run test:visual` snapshots `/design` at 375, 768 and 1280 px, light and dark, against committed baselines; it needs a browser and is not part of `gate:local`. The colour ratchet fails on an empty scan and exempts the open-graph routes, the contact email HTML and the token declarations in `app/globals.css` through one allowlist; its baseline is now 791. The `globals.css` loader test scans the whole repo and catches dynamic `import()`, `require` and CSS `@import`. Existing pages render unchanged; the compiled stylesheet is byte-identical. Tests: `tests/unit/design-page-190.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/design-contrast-190.test.ts`, `tests/unit/globals-consolidation-189.test.ts` (#190)

title: a design-system token layer and a current-UI audit
description: a design-system token layer and a current-UI audit. `app/globals.css` gains semantic `--ds-*` tokens between `#188 design-system tokens` markers: surface, text, border, accent, status and S–D score-band colours as HSL components with light (`:root`) and dark (`.dark`) values, plus type scale, spacing, radius, shadow and motion (durations drop to 0ms under reduced motion). They map in `tailwind.config.js` as `bg-ds-surface`, `text-ds-text-muted`, `text-ds-body`, `p-ds-md`, `rounded-ds-card`, `shadow-ds-md`, `duration-ds-base` and so on. Nothing uses them yet, so pages render unchanged; every listed text/surface pair meets WCAG AA in both modes. `docs/refresh/design-tokens.md` is the reference and the component API notes for #190; `docs/refresh/design-audit/` holds the token inventory and the per-file list of 845 hard-coded colours. `scripts/design-audit-shots.ts` captures 9 page types at 375/768/1280 px in light and dark into gitignored `tmp/design-audit/<label>/` and compares two sets; `scripts/build-design-swatches.ts` writes the swatch page `tmp/design-swatches.html`. title: the daily-news cron (/api/cron/daily-news, CRON_SECRET-gated) regenerates the current month's what's-new summary after…
description: the daily-news cron (`/api/cron/daily-news`, `CRON_SECRET`-gated) regenerates the current month's what's-new summary after ingestion, so the page no longer shows an old month until an admin regenerates it. Each run makes at most one LLM call, and skips it when the month's data hash matches the stored summary, when the month has no articles yet (the previous month's summary stays served), when under 60 s of the run's time budget remains, or when the ingestion run failed (`reason: "ingestion-failed"`, so a failed run spends no LLM credit). An LLM or database failure leaves every stored summary unchanged; the run still succeeds and reports it in `data.whatsNewSummary`. Whitespace-only LLM output is now rejected instead of stored. The public GET still never generates, and the admin POST is unchanged. The ingestion pipeline timeout drops from 10 minutes to 265 s, inside the cron's 300 s function limit: a run that exceeds it is marked failed and returns a result instead of being killed by Vercel with its run row left "running". Ingestion has priority: the summary step runs only when at least 60 s remain, and otherwise skips before any database read and retries the next day. The timeout path's failed-run write is limited to 10 s; a write that fails or hangs is reported in the run's `errors`. The admin summary POST's `maxDuration` rises from 60 s to 300 s, matching `/api/cron/monthly-summary`. Tests: `tests/unit/whats-new-auto-regenerate.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cron-daily-news-summary.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cron-daily-news-timeout.test.ts` (#160).

description: `scripts/check-ingestion-gap.mjs` could say a run ingested articles but not whether any of them reached the feed, which is exactly what the 2026-09-07 06:00 UTC run needed answering. Every outcome now also prints a detail block for the latest run: `INGESTED_ARTICLE_IDS=<count>` plus one `INGESTED_ARTICLE` line per recorded id joined to its `articles` row (`slug`, `status`, `published_date`, `created_at` — `slug=null` means no row matched the id at all, since `articles.slug` is NOT NULL), then `CANDIDATE_OUTCOMES=<total>`, one `CANDIDATE_OUTCOME` line per distinct outcome with its count, and one `CANDIDATE_INGESTED` line per `ingested` candidate carrying its URL and every date field the outcome recorded (`sourceDate`, `provisionalDate`, `effectiveDate`, `publishedDateSource`). The block is strictly appended and strictly additive: `withRunDetail()` copies `ok`/`exitCode` rather than recomputing them, so diagnosis cannot turn the gap check red or green, and `OK:`/`ALERT[...]`/`LAST_STATUS=`/`LAST_RUN_STARTED=` keep their exact text and position for the greps in `cron-gap-detector.yml`, which is otherwise unchanged. A run row predating migration 0013 — or a database without those columns, which the `to_jsonb(r) -> 'col'` projection reduces to NULL instead of an error — prints `unavailable` rather than failing, and a detail query that throws prints one `DETAIL_ERROR=` line. Anything URL-shaped is stripped from error text (this repository is public and the output is pasted into an issue body), candidate URLs are truncated to 120 characters and cannot inject a newline or a forged `ALERT[...]` into the log the workflow greps, and each list is capped at 50 lines with the overflow reported as a count (#138)
